subject: Tokenspeed SLA calibration and packaging
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tokenspeed SLA calibration and packaging

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table for how Redwood can bind a tokens/sec guarantee to a Dedicated GPU pool commit and a simple packaging/credit schedule to unblock procurement. This is deliberately prescriptive so procurement has something concrete to react to.

High-level measurement approach (attached: tokenspec-test-plan.pdf, bench-config.yaml):
- Metric definitions:
  - "Tokens/sec" = aggregate output tokens produced by the service per wall-clock second during a steady-state sample window (does not double-count cached prefixes).
  - "Requests/sec" (RPS) reported for visibility but primary commercial guarantee will be tokens/sec at the commit level.
- Latency targets: P95 end-to-end generation latency target for common payloads (<512 tokens) = 200ms; P99 target = 400ms. We can param different bands for long-seq workloads.
- Measurement harness: 3 x 30-minute steady-state windows (after a 10-minute warmup) across representative prompt sets (we'll run both synthetic and replayed production traces). Results are aggregated; lowest steady-state TPS across the three windows is the acceptance figure.
- Batching & cache policy: bench-config specifies concurrency, request multiplexing, and KV-cache warm/cold scenarios. Batches are allowed — bench ties batch size/config to realistic client behavior.

Commercial packaging proposal (example bands for a 12-GPU pool):
- Band A (Committed tokens/sec >= 1,200k): 15% commit discount + SLA credit pool.
- Band B (Committed tokens/sec 900k–1,199k): 10% commit discount + reduced credit.
- Band C (<900k): no discount; short-term remediation plan.

SLA credit mechanics (simple, transparent):
- If measured tokens/sec during acceptance < committed band for two consecutive monthly reporting windows, Redwood issues credits pro-rated to the shortfall for that monthly billing period. 
- Credits capped at 30% of monthly commit for severe regressions; smaller misses get smaller pro-rata credits.

Next steps I propose: Redwood runs a quick acceptance bench with Acme's sample traffic (if you can provide a ~24-hour replay) or we run synthetic traces using the attached config. If you like the approach, Ben can scope the test harness and Laura will draft the SOW and credit schedule for DocuSign.

Attached: tokenspec-test-plan.pdf, bench-config.yaml

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tokenspeed SLA calibration and packaging

Thanks, Jasmine — this is very helpful and close to what procurement needs. A few clarifying items before we show finance: 

1) How do you account for mixed-sequence-length traffic in the tokens/sec guarantee? Our peak mixes include many short assistant-style prompts and a smaller set of long summarization jobs.
2) Batching can artificially inflate tokens/sec; will your measurement harness surface an “effective batch” metric and show how that maps to observed client latency?
3) We need to see the exact credit math. Example: if committed band = 1,200k tokens/sec and measured steady-state = 1,050k, what is the credit calculation for that month?
4) Can you provide a short run (30–60m) against a replay sample we upload? We have an internal spreadsheet of questions and examples — attached (acme-sla-questions.xlsx).

Also: what happens if hardware availability causes a temporary degradation during a monthly window (maintenance, host failures)? Is there an exclusion carve-out in measurement windows?

If you can answer the above and give us a runnable harness we can sign off quickly.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
VP, Infrastructure — Acme Retail
alyssa@acme-retail.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tokenspeed SLA calibration and packaging

Looping in a couple of negotiation details we should propose to Acme. I did a quick cost/credit sensitivity and recommend a tiered credit schedule that aligns with commit size (attached: negotiation-summary.pdf). Key points: 

- Mixed workloads: define three canonical profiles (short, medium, long) and run acceptance across a weighted mix that mirrors Acme's production distribution. The tokens/sec we guarantee will be the weighted aggregate across the profile mix (this prevents gaming by only running short-prompt batches).

- Batching: measurement harness will report both raw tokens/sec and "client-observed latency" (p95) at target concurrency. Batching is allowed but we will show the tradeoff table so Acme can choose a preferred operating point.

- Credit math (example): commit = 1,200k tokens/sec. Measured steady-state = 1,050k => shortfall = 150k (12.5%). Credit = pro-rated share of monthly commit x shortfall% x agreed rate factor. In negotiation we can simplify to a lookup table (e.g., shortfall 5–15% => 10% credit; 15–30% => 20% credit) to avoid per-token calculations.

- Exclusions: maintenance windows or host failure incidents that are recorded in our incident log and agreed root-cause classified as infrastructure maintenance (vs. systemic regressions) will be excluded from measurement windows; we record and share logs for transparency.

Operational ask: if Acme can provide a 24-hour replay of a representative day, we will run the 3x30m steady-state harness against it and return an acceptance report (and the raw CSVs) within 48 hours. Otherwise we run synthetic traces that match their profile.

Proposed negotiation posture to present to Acme: offer an initial 3-month ramp at Band B pricing with an option to re-evaluate after 90 days based on observed usage and measured steady-state. That gets finance comfortable and gives us data.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Alyssa — thanks for the detailed questions and the spreadsheet. Quick answers inline and a proposed next step so procurement can move: 

On Tue, Jun 7, 2027 at 08:34 AM Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acme-retail.com> wrote:
> 1) How do you account for mixed-sequence-length traffic...
We will test with a weighted profile derived from your replay (or if you prefer, our recommended default mix: 70% short, 25% medium, 5% long). Tokens/sec guarantee will be the weighted aggregate across that mix.

> 2) Batching can artificially inflate tokens/sec; will your measurement harness surface an “effective batch” metric...
Yes — bench-config outputs per-window: raw tokens/sec, effective batch size distribution, and client-observed p95/p99 latencies. We'll include the CSVs so you can reproduce the figures.

> 3) We need to see the exact credit math...
Ben included the proposed pragmatic lookup-table above. Laura will draft a readable credit schedule for the SOW so procurement has clear examples (we'll avoid per-token billing math in the contract).

> 4) Can you provide a short run (30–60m) against a replay sample we upload?
Yes — please upload the 24h sample to the secure S3 link in the HubSpot deal (I've cc'd Laura; she will share upload instructions). If you only want a quick health check, we can run a 1-hour synthetic short-run first.

> Maintenance exclusion
We exclude scheduled maintenance and documented host failure incidents from the monthly measurement window; the SOW will include a clause describing documented exclusions and the evidence required.

Proposed operational next step:
- Acme uploads a 24-hour replay OR we agree to a scheduled 1-hour quick-run this week.
- Laura will send a draft SOW + simple credit table via DocuSign (link below) for procurement review.

DocuSign SOW draft: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/SOW-ACME-8347
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8347

If this looks good I'll coordinate dates and Ben will own the bench run and acceptance report.

Thanks —
Jasmine
